title: Interpersonal Communication (or ENGL C1000 / COMM C1000)
description: This course explores the symbolic nature of communication (verbal and nonverbal) that creates, maintains, and transforms the self and other in relational contexts. The examination of power, privilege, culture, history, gender, society, and media and technology are grounded in the theories and research of social and behavioral sciences.
outcomes: Describe and explain how communication creates, develops, and changes personal identities, including variables such as, gender, sex, race, culture, history, ethnicity, and class; explain the effect of communication on personal identities.
Describe the effects of communication on interpersonal relationships and social and cultural realities.
Analyze and evaluate ethical interpersonal communication founded on human communication theories and social science research and understand the implications in interpersonal dynamics.
Interrogate systems and discursive practices that uphold oppression and how human communication processes can dismantle oppressive practices and advocate for a more equitable and inclusive society.
Analyze conflict in interpersonal relationships and apply appropriate conflict management strategies.
content: Model of communication and definition of interpersonal communication
Self-concept and Self-Fulfilling Prophecy (gender and culture)
assignments: Reading textbook, case studies and other articles as assigned.
Collaborative group project and paper on interpersonal and/or related
Video or multi-media analysis using interpersonal communication concepts
Personal reflection papers - analyzing a communication situation or applying and
Research paper or project on a concept related to interpersonal communication
notes: no objectives section in this format; units 3
